chunks: And it is narrated: that Jibrīl عليه السلام descended upon the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله in a black cloak and a belt in which there was a dagger.

So he صلى الله عليه وآله said: “O Jibrīl, what is this attire?” He said: “The attire of the children of your uncle al-ʿAbbās, O Muḥammad. Woe to your progeny from the progeny of your uncle al-ʿAbbās.”

Then the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله went out to al-ʿAbbās and said: “O uncle, woe to my progeny from your progeny.” He said: “O Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, should I cut off myself?” He said: “The Pen has run with what is in it.”

key_terms.جَبْرَئِيلُ: Jibrīl, the angel who brings divine messages
key_terms.جَرَى الْقَلَمُ: the Pen has run, indicating what has been divinely decreed
key_terms.وَيْلٌ: woe, an expression of grave warning

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith about Jibrīl’s black attire and the descendants of al-ʿAbbās mean?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates a symbolic descent of Jibrīl عليه السلام before the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله, bearing a form of dress associated with the descendants of al-ʿAbbās. It conveys a forewarning of future harm that would come upon the Prophet’s progeny from that branch, and closes by affirming the finality of divine decree.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.769 - It is narrated that Archangel Jibril, descended upon the Messenger of Allah (sw) wearing a black cloak and a belt with a dagger.

The Prophet (sw) asked: "O’ Archangel Jibril (as), what is this attire?"
Archangel Jibril (as) replied: "It is the attire of your uncle's descendants, O’ Muhammad. Woe to your progeny from the progeny of your uncle al-Abbas."

The Prophet (sw) then went out to al-Abbas and said: "O’ uncle, woe to my progeny from your progeny."
Al-Abbas asked: "O’ Messenger of Allah (sw), should I end myself (to prevent this)?"
The Prophet replied: "The Pen has decreed what is to come."
